advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Keep each stream's existing error handler when reconfiguring: `stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors=stream.errors)`
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:315: for name in ("stdin", "stdout", "stderr"):
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:321: stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
CPython TextIOWrapper.reconfigure: if encoding is given and errors is None, errors becomes 'strict' (the old handler is kept only when encoding is also None).
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:350: sys.stderr.write(str(e) + "\n") — the error-rendering path that would now be strict-encoded
advisory.finding: `_use_utf8_stdio` calls `stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")` without passing `errors=`. CPython's `TextIOWrapper.reconfigure` resets the error handler to 'strict' whenever an encoding is given without one. So on any host where the stream is re-encoded, sys.stderr loses Python's default 'backslashreplace' (and stdin/stdout lose 'surrogateescape' where it was set). A diagnostic that contains a lone surrogate (for example an `os.fsdecode` path) will then raise UnicodeEncodeError while the error is being written, hiding the original error.
scenarios: Windows piped stderr (cp1252, backslashreplace) is switched to utf-8/strict; an error message carrying a surrogate-escaped path then crashes the error write.
Linux with a non-UTF-8 locale (e.g. LANG=en_US.ISO-8859-1): stderr is switched to utf-8 and the backslashreplace guarantee is lost.

It only inspects `<obj>.run(...)` calls whose `text=` keyword is the literal `True`, and it returns `[]` when it finds no such call. If a file in `_CLI_CONSUMERS` moves to `check_output`, `Popen`, `universal_newlines=True`, a bare imported `run(...)`, or a wrapper helper, the test still passes. 'Every call names UTF-8' then looks the same as 'the scan found nothing to check'.
scenarios: A refactor routes `rebar list --full` through `subprocess.check_output(..., text=True)` with no encoding; the regression guard stays green while Windows decoding breaks again.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have `_text_mode_runs_without_utf8` return `(inspected, missing)` and assert `inspected > 0 and missing == []`. Match `func.attr`/`func.id` in {"run", "check_output", "Popen"} and treat `universal_newlines=True` like `text=True`.

advisory.finding: test_rebar_cli_output_is_decoded_as_utf8 tests the source text of the five CLI-consumer modules, not their behaviour. It ast-parses each production file and checks that every `.run(...)` call with a literal `text=True` also has a literal `encoding="utf-8"` kwarg. It breaks on behaviour-preserving refactors, such as passing `encoding=_UTF8` or `encoding="UTF-8"`. It also passes trivially when the call moves into a shared helper or uses `universal_newlines=True`/`**kwargs`, because the helper then finds no matching node and returns an empty list.
scenarios: Someone refactors pass_support.py to call a shared `_run_cli(argv, **kw)` helper that hard-codes `text=True` and leaves out encoding. The scan finds no `text=True` literal at the call site and stays green while Windows decoding regresses.
Someone replaces `encoding="utf-8"` with a module constant `encoding=UTF8`. Behaviour is the same, but the test goes red.
advisory.suggested_fix: Test the behaviour instead, as the hook test already does: run each consumer's subprocess path in a child under `-X warn_default_encoding -W error::EncodingWarning`, or monkeypatch `subprocess.run` at the boundary and assert the `encoding` kwarg the consumer passes. If the structural scan stays, add a liveness anchor such as `assert found_calls` so a file with no matching calls cannot pass trivially.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Limit `_use_utf8_stdio` to non-TTY (piped) streams or Windows, respect an explicit `PYTHONIOENCODING`, and give stdin a tolerant `errors=` handler.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py: `for name in ("stdin", "stdout", "stderr"): ... if isinstance(stream, io.TextIOWrapper) and stream.encoding.lower() not in ("utf-8", "utf8"): stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")`
No `isatty()` check, no `PYTHONIOENCODING` check and no `errors=` argument, so stdin decoding stays strict.

tests/unit/test_windows_text_encoding.py `test_rebar_explain_writes_utf8_through_a_cp1252_stdout` asserts that an explicit `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252` is overridden, confirming the user's choice is ignored.
advisory.finding: `_use_utf8_stdio` forces UTF-8 on stdin, stdout and stderr whenever the encoding is not already UTF-8. It does this even for interactive TTYs whose user locale is deliberately non-UTF-8 (for example ISO-8859-1 or EUC-JP terminals) and even when the user explicitly set `PYTHONIOENCODING`. Non-ASCII output then renders as mojibake on those terminals. Non-UTF-8 piped input, such as Windows PowerShell 5.1 piping in the ANSI code page, raises `UnicodeDecodeError` under the strict handler that `reconfigure` keeps.
scenarios: A user on a Linux terminal with a legacy-charset locale runs `rebar explain plan` and sees garbled non-ASCII glyphs such as the em dash.
`Get-Content notes.txt | rebar ...` in Windows PowerShell 5.1 pipes cp1252 text; reading stdin raises `UnicodeDecodeError`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `errors="replace"` (at least for diagnostic stderr) to the new UTF-8 `subprocess.run` decodes, or catch `UnicodeDecodeError` alongside `OSError`/`SubprocessError`.
evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/conflict_bug_filing.py: `res = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=False, timeout=30)` followed by `except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:`. `UnicodeDecodeError` is not caught.
src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_dry_run.py:240 and :345 add `encoding="utf-8"` to git and rebar-CLI `subprocess.run` calls with no `errors=` argument.
src/rebar/reconciler/invariant_sink.py:71, pass_support.py:226 and run_differs.py:135 apply the same strict decode to child output.
advisory.finding: Several parents now decode child output with strict `encoding="utf-8"` and no `errors=` handler, but their exception handlers do not catch `UnicodeDecodeError`. Any non-UTF-8 byte in a child's stdout or stderr would therefore crash the caller instead of degrading. Such bytes could come from localized git or tool messages or from an older rebar child still writing cp1252. Previously, on Windows, cp1252 decoding almost never failed.
scenarios: A version-skewed rebar child, or a tool emitting localized ANSI-code-page stderr on Windows, writes byte 0x97. `subprocess.run` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` and aborts the reconciler pass or the bug filing.
advisory.suggested_fix: Pass `errors="replace"` alongside `encoding="utf-8"` in the `subprocess.run` calls whose output is used for diagnostics or fail-open parsing. For example, in conflict_bug_filing.py: `subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", check=False, timeout=30)`.
